title: A foreign session id is answered 404, never 403
rationale: The per-session reads take no tenant param: the id is the request. The check therefore runs on the fetched row, and the response for a session that belongs to another tenant must be identical to the response for a session that does not exist. A 403 here would confirm the id is real, turning the endpoint into an existence oracle and letting a caller enumerate another tenant's session ids without reading a single row. This is the request-shaped expression of the same rule ContentState.UNAVAILABLE encodes in the schema.

contract.note: Must match the 404 for a wholly invented id, both in status and in body shape.
